\subsection{S1.1 Implementation and core-metric
pseudocode}\label{s1.1-implementation-and-core-metric-pseudocode}

All models run in evaluation mode. M3 computes chunked VJPs with
torch.autograd.grad in is\_grads\_batched mode and frozen
gradient\_chunk\_size=16. Evidence JSON files record random seeds, model
and image hashes, worker environments, and per-task times. Table S2
reports scan time, throughput, memory, and retained storage; the 456
supplemental-control tasks total 2.4502 GPU-hours. Core implementations
reside in src/vitnns/endpoint\_m3\_atlas.py, src/vitnns/endpoint\_m4.py,
and the corresponding scripts/run\_endpoint\_*.py entry points.

\begin{verbatim}
Endpoint(s, x):
    g <- VJP(s, x) at the observed forward state
    return x * g

StructuredCut(F, edges, reconstruction_target):
    for each actual use-edge z_k in a valid cut:
        g_k <- downstream cotangent dF/dz_k
        E_k <- x * VJP(z_k, x; vector=g_k)
    assert sum_k E_k closes to reconstruction_target # branch contribution or Total Endpoint

SpatialMetrics(E, target_patch):
    M[p] <- sum_rgb abs(E[p, rgb])
    if sum_p M[p] == 0: return NA
    p_patch <- patch_sum(M) / sum_p M[p]
    entropy <- -sum_j p_patch[j] log(p_patch[j]) / log(196)
    locality <- neighborhood_mass(target_patch) - uniform_neighborhood_mass
    distance <- sum_j p_patch[j] normalized_distance(j, target_patch)

RandomRegionAUC(repeats):
    for each random repeat r:
        curve_r <- absolute finite effect at every area budget
        auc_r <- trapezoid(curve_r, area in [0, 0.25]) / 0.25
    return mean_r auc_r
\end{verbatim}

CLS has no natural target patch, so locality and target-relative
distance are defined only for patch-token targets; zero-mass cases
propagate as NA. Tokens, channels, and heads are aggregated within each
image by prespecified rules before image-level inference.

\section{S2. Frozen decisions and numerical
diagnostics}\label{s2.-frozen-decisions-and-numerical-diagnostics}

C4a: BROAD\_BUT\_NON\_UNIVERSAL\_FAMILY\_LEVEL\_SUPPORT; original
all-family omnibus NOT\_SUPPORTED. C4b: NOT\_SUPPORTED. The numerical
atlas status is
PASS\_FLOAT64\_RECOVERY\_WITH\_RETAINED\_FLOAT32\_FAILURE: 36/57,600
float32 failures are retained and 36/36 same-coordinate float64 checks
pass. These fields are not interchangeable.

\section{S3. Reference sensitivity}\label{s3.-reference-sensitivity}

Change uses atol=1e-12 and rtol=0. Relative change is
abs(q0-qblur)/max(abs(q0),abs(qblur)); both-zero denominators are NA.
Component quantiles describe the pooled records, not independent
inferential samples.

Head rankings use average ranks and Kendall tau-b. Top-K ties are broken
by ascending component ID; Top-3 overlap is intersection size / 3. Rank
displacement uses original rank positions, so model head counts affect
its scale. Each image averages 12 blocks, then summaries use 400 images.
Full-order equality counts are Taylor 0/4,800 and effect 0/4,800 for
ViT-B, Taylor 46/4,800 and effect 64/4,800 for DeiT-S.

\section{S5. Corrected absolute random AUC and
oracle}\label{s5.-corrected-absolute-random-auc-and-oracle}

The current random baseline takes absolute effects before integration
within each repeat, then averages AUCs. Corrected results, repeat
distributions and MC stability are in
\href{supplement_experiments_v1.md}{supplementary experiments S9}. The
old analysis is retained as a historical reconstruction of its original
estimand.

\section{S6. Detailed attention/residual evidence (historical stage
identifiers
retained)}\label{s6.-detailed-attentionresidual-evidence-historical-stage-identifiers-retained}

\subsection{Historical M4: attention routing/value and residual
mechanisms}\label{historical-m4-attention-routingvalue-and-residual-mechanisms}

M4 covered a shared 400-image cohort, both models, all 12 blocks, and
every head for the frozen ground-truth logit. The result contains 86,400
image-block-head attention records, 19,200 image-block-residual records,
and 691,200 direction-head JVP records. Per-head Q+K+V reconstructed the
native attention Endpoint, routing+value reconstructed the same object,
and identity/carry plus branch reconstructed the full logit Endpoint at
both residual additions.

The independent CPU audit recomputed 230,400 E3 summary fields. Maximum
absolute Q/K/V and residual closure errors were 1.574e-05 and 2.480e-05.
The maximum relative error between the explicit attention differential
and native JVP was 2.502e-05. All 19,200 identity/carry omission
controls failed closure as intended, and 384 attention-detach block
checks passed for the first 16 frozen evaluation orders.

\subsubsection{Review-R2 sensitivity and estimand
refinement}\label{review-r2-sensitivity-and-estimand-refinement}

Review-R2 tested whether the large late-block Value-only JVP
discrepancies were driven by small denominators. At block 11, the median
relative discrepancies were 0.9516 for ViT-B/16 and 0.9636 for
DeiT-S/16; the corresponding full-response denominators were 14.9711 and
1.5155, while absolute discrepancies were 13.8064 and 1.4228. The
discrepancies therefore occur at the same norm scale as the full
response rather than arising generally from near-zero denominators.

\refstepcounter{figure}\label{fig:en-supplement-001}
\pandocbounded{\includegraphics[keepaspectratio,alt={M4 Review Archived R2 Figure 1}]{../supplement/S77_supp_m4_review_01_m4_review_jvp_diagnostics.png}}

\textbf{M4 Review Archived R2 Figure 1.} Block-11 distributions of
normalized JVP discrepancy, absolute discrepancy, and full-response
denominator for both models.

After adjustment for head projection-input activation norm and
downstream-cotangent norm, mean-query saturation remained negatively
associated with routing share, Endpoint error, and JVP error in both
models. The fully adjusted correlations were −0.1442/−0.3257,
−0.1129/−0.2185, and −0.1453/−0.2786 for ViT-B/16 and DeiT-S/16,
respectively. CLS-query relations were weaker: the adjusted ViT-B
routing-share and Endpoint-error tests had Holm \(p=0.0629\). The
supported summary therefore concerns all-query mean saturation, with the
association concentrated in early and middle blocks.

\refstepcounter{figure}\label{fig:en-supplement-002}
\pandocbounded{\includegraphics[keepaspectratio,alt={M4 Review Archived R2 Figure 2}]{../supplement/S78_supp_m4_review_02_m4_review_saturation_robustness.png}}

\textbf{M4 Review Archived R2 Figure 2.} Unadjusted and partial-rank
saturation relations, including phase-level sensitivity and the weaker
CLS-query result.

The full-cohort spatial analysis measured total variation between output
and identity 14×14 patch absolute distributions. Attention residual
late-minus-early differences were +0.0520 ({[}0.0488, 0.0547{]}) for
ViT-B/16 and +0.0282 ({[}0.0257, 0.0300{]}) for DeiT-S/16; MLP residual
differences were −0.0187 ({[}−0.0220, −0.0150{]}) and −0.0462
({[}−0.0516, −0.0412{]}). All four post-hoc sensitivity tests survived
Holm correction. Branch-relative path scale and spatial TV were
positively associated within images across blocks.

\refstepcounter{figure}\label{fig:en-supplement-003}
\pandocbounded{\includegraphics[keepaspectratio,alt={M4 Review Archived R2 Figure 3}]{../supplement/S79_supp_m4_review_03_m4_review_residual_spatial.png}}

\textbf{M4 Review Archived R2 Figure 3.} Full-cohort residual
spatial-change sensitivity for attention and MLP sublayers.

On 16 pre-retained class-logit maps per model, Full--Value patch TV rose
from 0.0550/0.0307 at block 0 to 0.1865/0.1811 at block 11. Its 12-block
trajectory was directionally compatible with M3 entropy, locality, and
distance, but M3 used 100-image token-channel targets with only one
overlapping image per model. This is a model-level trajectory bridge,
not a unit-level or causal link between routing and spatial broadening.

\refstepcounter{figure}\label{fig:en-supplement-004}
\pandocbounded{\includegraphics[keepaspectratio,alt={M4 Review Archived R2 Figure 4}]{../supplement/S80_supp_m4_review_04_m4_review_m3_m4_bridge.png}}

\textbf{M4 Review Archived R2 Figure 4.} Descriptive bridge between M3
spatial trajectories and full-versus-Value class-logit map differences.

\subsubsection{Figures}\label{figures}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Image \#1 (m4\_attention\_depth): routing share, frozen-attention
  Endpoint error, and eight-direction JVP error across blocks; bands are
  10,000-replicate image-bootstrap 95\% intervals.
\item
  Image \#2 (m4\_attention\_saturation): descriptive block-level
  locations of saturation versus routing/error; formal association tests
  use within-image, within-layer head Spearman correlations.
\item
  Image \#3 (m4\_residual\_depth): identity share, path cancellation,
  and spatial TV for attention and MLP residuals.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection{Interpretation boundary}\label{interpretation-boundary}

M4 quantifies local Jacobian path accounting at the observed input for
the frozen ground-truth logit. A larger routing share or branch mass
indicates more local input dependence along that path; causal importance
requires separate finite-intervention evidence.

\section{S9. Correction of the random-region
baseline}\label{s9.-correction-of-the-random-region-baseline}

Each random repetition takes the absolute effect before AUC integration;
its AUC is then averaged over 20 repetitions and heads within an image.
The legacy estimator averaged signed curves first and underestimated
absolute-effect random performance through cancellation. The table
reports medians and paired median differences for 400-image families,
with 2,000 image-bootstrap intervals.

\begin{equation}\label{eq:en-supplement-001}
\widehat A_{\rm random}=\frac1R\sum_{r=1}^R\frac1{0.25}\int_0^{0.25}|e_r(a)|\,da.
\end{equation}

The median per-image relative Monte Carlo SE is 5.1\%--6.9\%, with q90
of 7.6\%--8.9\%. Resampling 5/10/20 repetitions from the observed pool
shows increasing error at smaller repetition counts. Conditional on the
fixed images, cohort-mean Monte Carlo variation is smaller than
image-sampling uncertainty; small single-image advantages remain poorly
resolved. This diagnostic covers the observed repetition pool and does
not establish that 20 repetitions meet every precision requirement.

\section{S10. Trained and randomly initialized
models}\label{s10.-trained-and-randomly-initialized-models}

Each ViT-B/16 and DeiT-S/16 architecture has three random states
(202609201, 202609202, 202609203), sharing the first 32 frozen M3
images, all 12 blocks, 16 tokens and 16 frozen channels per block with
the trained model; M4 includes all heads. Random states use the same
timm 0.9.16 architecture and native initialization, and each state is
fixed across images. Trained statistics are selected from existing M3/M4
raw arrays for the identical images and targets. Units are aggregated
within images; early=0--3 and late=8--11. Trained-minus-random intervals
independently resample shared images and initialization seeds in 2,000
crossed-bootstrap draws.

Random models already show increasing entropy and distance and
decreasing locality, so spatial broadening is not unique to the trained
parameter state. Trained entropy late-minus-early is 0.2288/0.2256,
compared with random-state means of 0.0940/0.1718; the two parameter
states differ in broadening magnitude. Routing scale increases in the
trained parameter states while its random-state mean trend is negative,
and attention identity changes in opposite directions between the two
states. MLP identity increases in both, with the ViT-B
trained-state-minus-random-state interval including zero. Three random
states limit inference over the initialization population; this
comparison does not identify a causal effect of training or separately
identify architecture and initialization effects.

\section{S11. Target robustness}\label{s11.-target-robustness}

The frozen M3 cohort supplies 100 images per model, with GT, clean-top1
and top1-minus-runnerup targets at blocks 0/5/11 and all heads. Class
indices are fixed on the clean input. Correct/incorrect counts are 92/8
for ViT-B and 86/14 for DeiT-S; GT and top1 are identical on correct
images. The table reports image-level B11-minus-B0 after head
aggregation for all/correct/incorrect groups. Targets within a group
share bootstrap image indices.

Routing scale and Value-only error increase with depth under all three
targets; attention identity decreases and MLP identity increases, with
consistent directions in correct and incorrect subsets. Margin targets
change magnitudes: ViT-B routing increases by 0.1439 rather than the GT
value of 0.2031, and DeiT-S attention identity changes by −0.1014 rather
than −0.2168. The incorrect subsets contain only 8/14 images, limiting
their precision.

Native attention-output JVPs depend on the model and input,
independently of the explained class, so their eight-direction
discrepancy is inherited from the identical original M4 images. The
additional target\_contracted\_jvp contracts directional derivatives
with each target cotangent at the head output and measures
target-dependent Value-only discrepancy. The two quantities are reported
separately. Saturation relations use within-block Spearman across heads;
their depth changes are reported alongside complete block values, target
contrasts and NA counts in the data files.

\section{S12. Quantitative feature--Endpoint
relationship}\label{s12.-quantitative-featureendpoint-relationship}

Each model uses 32 frozen images, 12 blocks and 16 frozen random
channels per block, giving 12,288 energy targets. The sum covers 196
patch tokens and excludes CLS, matching the energy definition in the
forward displays. Raw RGB Endpoint absolute mass is aggregated to
patches; display normalization and spatial-variance channel selection do
not enter the analysis.

\begin{equation}\label{eq:en-supplement-002}
s_{b,c}=\frac12\sum_{t=1}^{196}h_{b,t,c}^2,\qquad
q_t=\frac{h_{b,t,c}^2}{\sum_{j=1}^{196}h_{b,j,c}^2},\qquad
p_t=\frac{\sum_{i\in P_t}|x_i\partial s_{b,c}/\partial x_i|}{\sum_i|x_i\partial s_{b,c}/\partial x_i|}.
\end{equation}

Mean image-level Spearman is 0.2663/0.2811 for correct pairing, with
positive paired-difference intervals against wrong-channel, cross-layer
same-channel, patch-permutation and random-channel controls. Cosine,
Jensen--Shannon distance and top-20 overlap are also reported.
Same-channel forward energy and local input dependence are associated
beyond these controls, with substantial departures from equivalence.
Channel and block medians are taken within each image before image-level
statistics.

\section{S13. Sampling sensitivity}\label{s13.-sampling-sensitivity}

The same 32 images reuse all original M3 32 channels and 15 patch
strata. Channel and token-stratum bootstraps use 256 draws each, image
bootstrap uses 2,000 draws, and each block or spatial stratum is omitted
in turn. The table gives resampling and deletion-sensitivity ranges. The
three spatial trend directions persist across all ranges. This
resampling analysis does not constitute independent channel-seed
replication. CLS-minus-patch is the all-layer difference; other metrics
are late-minus-early.

\section{S14. Cross-layer all-head M2 and
scope}\label{s14.-cross-layer-all-head-m2-and-scope}

The main block-5 three-head experiment corresponds to the original
confirmatory protocol. Sealed M2 covers blocks 2/5/10, two models, all
heads, two references and 400 images per family. Under native patch
geometry, 11/12 full-input and 12/12 isolated-head families favor
regional Taylor. The table retains Holm correction over the original 672
bidirectional AUC tests.

Optional cascading randomization, the P2 same-target M3--M4 bridge,
independent channel seeds and alternative checkpoints, and P3 input
transforms and CNN display were not executed. Training controls concern
local parameter-dependent structure; different scalar targets do not
form a unit-matched finite causal mechanism. Original Path-IG
calibration failure and confirmatory decisions are retained.

\# S15. Data, models, populations, and analysis identities

ImageNet data come from the official ILSVRC2012 validation set. Models
instantiate timm 0.9.16 standard Block/Attention and strictly load
checkpoint keys. All checkpoint byte counts and SHA-256 values were
recomputed. AugReg names identify IN21K pretraining followed by IN1K
fine-tuning or IN1K training; DeiT-S uses public Facebook IN1K weights.
Results condition on these parameter states.

Discovery, calibration, and evaluation contain 64, 64, and 400 classes,
respectively, with one image per class. The 100-class unit study is an
evaluation subset. E1 has five images from each of 100 classes; E5 has
one from each of 400 classes. E5 uses class\_e5/image\_e5 hash ordering
after excluding historical exposures and E1. The matrix reports image
identity overlap. Classes may recur across later cohorts; independent
images do not imply independent classes. E5 train/validation/test labels
belong to a separate prediction analysis and do not change this
all-400-image H1--H4 check.

Preprocessing uses Pillow 10.2.0 RGB without EXIF transpose. Torchvision
0.17.2 resizes the PIL image's shorter side to 248 with bicubic
interpolation and antialias=True, center-crops to 224, converts to
float32, and divides by 255. Table 2 specifies model normalization. Blur
operates after cropping in RGB with a 31×31 Gaussian kernel, sigma=10,
and reflect padding=15, then normalizes. Evaluation mode disables
dropout and drop path. CLS, positions, and biases are fixed. The
original logit target uses the official ground-truth class; clean-top1
is a separate frozen readout. Neither determines cohort selection. The
original registry records its four-token/four-channel per-block
selections. M3 fixes CLS plus 15 tokens from 3×5 spatial strata and 32
channels per block. Equal cross-model channel indices do not imply
semantic correspondence. Structural analysis scans all heads and 12
blocks; the primary regional task fixes block 5 with ViT-B heads 0/6/11
and DeiT-S heads 0/3/5.

Selections use deterministic rules or explicit seeds. Actual IDs and
targets appear in
\href{../evidence/revision_v6/cohort_bindings.json}{cohort bindings}.
Original protocols retain exact random-control keys and invocation
order; seeds from different analyses are not interchangeable.

\# S16. Finite-replacement variables and executable pseudocode

A and V are forward variables; routing-induced/value-induced are
differential partitions. Table 6's A/V family contains one all-head A
and one all-head V replacement per block, totaling 24 components. Head
families include all block/head pairs; residual families contain
attention and MLP branches per block. Reference activations come from a
complete reference forward. The consumer slot is part of replacement
identity.

\begin{verbatim}
clean_rgb = RGB(image) / 255
clean_rgb = center_crop(resize_shorter_side(clean_rgb, 248, bicubic, antialias=True), 224)
x = (clean_rgb - mu) / sigma
reference_zero = zeros_like(x)             # raw RGB equals mu
reference_blur = (GaussianBlur(clean_rgb, kernel=31, sigma=10, reflect_padding=15) - mu) / sigma
clean = forward_and_capture(x)
reference = forward_and_capture(reference_input)
for fixed block, component, consumer slot:
    replacement = reference.tensor_at(component, slot)
    patched = forward(x, replace_only_this_use=replacement)
    effect = clean.GT_logit - patched.GT_logit
    # All sibling heads and bypass inputs remain clean before the replacement.
    # Every node downstream of the replaced use is recomputed normally.

for singleton region P in the fixed 4x4 grid of 56x56 pixels:
    x_P = x.copy(); x_P[P] = reference_input[P]
    mixed[P] = forward_and_capture(x_P)
    regional_Taylor[P] = abs(dot(clean_head_cotangent, clean_head - mixed[P].head))
rank_regions(score, ties=ascending_region_id)
for budget in [1, 2, 4]:
    selected = top_regions(budget)
    x_selected = x with selected pixels from reference_input
    mixed = forward_and_capture(x_selected)
    full_input_effect = clean.GT_logit - mixed.GT_logit
    isolated = forward(x, target_head_slice=mixed.head_slice)
    isolated_effect = clean.GT_logit - isolated.GT_logit
AUC = trapezoid(abs(isolated_effect), areas=[0,1/16,2/16,4/16]) / 0.25
image_AUC = mean(AUC across the three fixed heads)
random_AUC = mean(AUC per random repeat, then heads) # abs before averaging repeats
\end{verbatim}

Full-input effects change the entire forward computation.
Isolated-component effects insert only the target tensor from a
mixed-input forward into a clean forward, preserving sibling heads and
bypass inputs. Candidate sets match across regional scores, but Taylor
requires singleton mixed forwards and therefore additional information.
Region ties use ascending IDs; head ties use ascending component IDs;
Spearman uses average ranks. Candidate-envelope AUC takes the greatest
evaluated absolute effect separately at each area, then integrates and
averages heads. It may join points from different rankings and is not an
executable globally optimal region policy. It supplies an upper envelope
over evaluated candidates and the regret denominator.

\# S17. Coordinate sensitivity and independent analytic checks

All representations use the same current input point, fixed target, and
checkpoint. Raw gradient divides by model sigma; the common-origin
weighted gradient uses raw RGB zero, independently of model mean. Cells
report image-level median differences and 95\% bootstrap intervals. Unit
n=100 and structural n=400 per model, with no missing images.
Coordinates are paired within images and are not additional samples.

\begin{equation}\label{eq:en-supplement-003}
E_i^{(x)}=x_i\frac{\partial s}{\partial x_i},\qquad
G_i^{(r)}=\frac1{\sigma_i}\frac{\partial s}{\partial x_i},\qquad
E_i^{(0)}=r_i\frac{\partial s}{\partial r_i}
=\left(x_i+\frac{\mu_i}{\sigma_i}\right)\frac{\partial s}{\partial x_i}.
\end{equation}

DeiT-S Q changes B11−B0 point-estimate sign across coordinates and all
three intervals cross zero. Differences between phase and endpoint
contrasts also show why an endpoint comparison cannot replace a
trajectory. Main claims remain restricted to normalized-input Endpoint.
Other objects support direction retention for these three
representations, not general parameterization invariance.

The independent NumPy float64 reference explicitly constructs affine,
LayerNorm, softmax \(\operatorname{diag}(a)-aa^{\mathsf T}\), Q/K/V,
head concatenation/output projection, GELU/MLP, and residual-identity
Jacobians. It imports no scanner, hooks, or autograd. A separate driver
compares reference maps with the actual main scanner on single-head,
double-head, and pre-LN residual attention/MLP tiny models. All 32
component comparisons and nine frozen-direction finite differences pass,
with maximum component absolute error \(1.11\times10^{-16}\).
Per-component relative L2 errors and tolerances appear in
\href{../evidence/revision_v6/analytic_reference_results.json}{analytic
results}. Shared-producer wrong-slot, attention Q/K-slot exchange,
premature fan-out merging, and duplicated merged terms are rejected
after the correct implementation passes. Coverage is limited to these
numerical graphs and fault types, rather than all possible scanner
errors.

The legacy regional key raw\_gradient stores \(\nabla_xs\), not
\(\nabla_rs\); the main text names its actual coordinates. Random region
order hashes the joined NNS\_VIT\_ENDPOINT\_E5\_RANDOM\_REGIONS\_V1,
task\_seed, model\_id, reference\_id, head, and repeat string with
SHA-256, uses its first eight big-endian bytes as the PCG64 seed, then
applies permutation(16). task\_seed derives from
NNS\_VIT\_ENDPOINT\_QUEUE\_V1 and task\_id.

A/V concordance is the fraction of 12 blocks with positive
\(\operatorname{sign}[(m_A-m_V)(|e_A|-|e_V|)]\); zero products are
excluded as ties. It is not Spearman and is reported descriptively
without a sign test against zero. The v7 r4 root contains complete
intervals, quantiles, per-block results, residual degrees of freedom,
condition numbers, and independent validation. Every required
correlation has 400/400 valid images.

The historical pooled association does not establish uniform within-type
ranking. V-only is stronger in ViT-B, while the DeiT-S normalized-zero
interval includes zero. MLP branches are positive in all four settings,
whereas attention branches are negative or near zero. After joint type
and block adjustment, A/V is near zero under both ViT-B references and
residual correlations are negative under normalized zero; DeiT-S
adjusted results change with reference.

All three radii retain the direction. Radius 1 remains the prespecified

The absolute-mass quartile diagnostic for residual output--identity TV
uses images as statistical units. Median attention TV from Q1 to Q4 is
0.107→0.073 for ViT-B and 0.071→0.055 for DeiT-S; MLP values are
0.139→0.105 and 0.117→0.090. Spatial differences are not confined to the
lowest-mass group, but this unadjusted post-hoc stratification does not
exclude gradient quality or noise effects.

H4 was independently recomputed from 1,600 raw JSON/NPZ pairs. Medians
for vit\_b16, deit\_s16, vit\_b16\_in1k, and vit\_s16\_augreg are
-0.114, -0.186, -0.186, and -0.136. Positive/negative/tie counts are
101/297/2, 96/298/6, 56/342/2, and 107/285/8. All within-checkpoint
Holm-adjusted values are below \(10^{-6}\). The v7 r4 root contains
per-image and block-level correlations, full-precision p values, and
machine receipts.

\section{S19. Architecture cuts, entropy quality, and H4 aggregation
sensitivity}\label{s19.-architecture-cuts-entropy-quality-and-h4-aggregation-sensitivity}

\subsection{S19.1 Three registries and certification of actual
cuts}\label{s19.1-three-registries-and-certification-of-actual-cuts}

The machine contracts now separate scalar targets, local-differential
decompositions, and finite-replacement interventions into three
read-only derived registries. Row-level recounting of the original EP0
target registry gives 457/385 scalar targets per image for ViT-B/16 and
DeiT-S/16, respectively. Each model has 192 post-block token-channel
coordinates, 48 patch sums, 48 patch energies, 18 module patch
aggregates, four patch-embedding aggregates, one final-CLS coordinate,
and two class logits; head-coordinate counts are 144 and 72.
Q/K/V-induced, routing/value, residual components, and intervenable
variables are not included in these totals.

\begingroup\scriptsize
\setlength{\tabcolsep}{2pt}
\begin{longtable}[]{@{}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 4\tabcolsep) * \real{0.3333}}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 4\tabcolsep) * \real{0.3333}}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 4\tabcolsep) * \real{0.3333}}@{}}

scalar target & Scalar readout, graph location, aggregation rule & Path
components and intervention variables \\
local-differential decomposition & Native use, analytic partition, cut,
reconstruction object & Scalar-target counts and finite-replacement
effects \\
finite-replacement intervention & Intervenable activation, reference,
effect, and regional task & Local-differential closure objects \\
\end{longtable}
\endgroup
}

The frozen pre-LN ViT tensor-use DAG checks all 80,832 combinations of
842 targets, 12 blocks, and eight cut declarations. Dynamic programming
over the target ancestor graph propagates the number of cut edges
crossed by every input path. A full cut requires that count set to be
exactly \(\{1\}\) and every declared edge to belong to the target
ancestor graph. Of the pairs, 26,094 pass the full target-cut condition,
15,660 pass the attention branch-only partition condition, 24,444 are
rejected because the declared reconstruction object is inapplicable, and
14,634 because the target is upstream or the branch is absent from its
ancestor graph. This proof covers the registry-bound standard unfused
pre-LN ViT; numerical closure and mutation tests remain separate
implementation evidence.

entropy}\label{s19.2-total-mass-sensitivity-of-spatial-entropy}

and block over all frozen M3 unit maps. The original late-minus-early
entropy is reproduced from source arrays with maximum error zero. The

retains all 100 images; quartile analyses propagate NA for a
legitimately empty cell.

Across model--block mass quartiles, ViT-B Q1--Q4 median differences are
0.090, 0.194, 0.238, and 0.266; DeiT-S values are 0.112, 0.205, 0.222,
and 0.224. Eight image--quartile cells have an empty early or late group
and are retained as typed NA, without deleting or replacing images.
Median within-image, within-block Spearman association between
log1p(total mass) and entropy is −0.729 {[}−0.747, −0.693{]} in ViT-B
and −0.760 {[}−0.775, −0.723{]} in DeiT-S. Late-minus-early log1p mass
is 2.893 {[}2.829, 2.961{]} and 2.183 {[}2.109, 2.227{]}. Entropy
therefore depends on map quality, while the overall broadening direction
is not produced solely by the lowest-mass maps.

\subsection{S19.3 H4 matched aggregation and random-region
precision}\label{s19.3-h4-matched-aggregation-and-random-region-precision}

The matched path score is
\(M^{\mathrm{sum}}_{jbh}=|\sum_i\mathcal L_{jbh,i}|\), giving it the
same sum-then-absolute aggregation order as the activation × gradient
comparator. The target, normalized-zero reference, four blocks,
finite-replacement effect, and image-level aggregation remain unchanged.

The original H4 is reproduced again from the same arrays with zero
per-image maximum error. All four checkpoints remain negative under
matched aggregation, so the absolute/sum ordering difference between
scores does not explain the original result.

No additional model run is needed for the random-region baseline. Source
validation covers 1,600 model--reference--image conditions and 32,000
repeat records, with all 20 repeats present in every condition. Median
relative Monte Carlo standard error is 5.1\%--6.9\%, with q90 of
7.6\%--8.9\%; 5/10/20-repeat resampling, split-half, and
leave-one-repeat-out diagnostics are retained. This precision supports
cohort-level comparisons; small single-image advantages are not decided
from it.
